title: Local Clustering on Complex Graphs and Complex Hypergraphs

problem.claim: Local/seeded clustering seeks a compact cluster near given starting instances.

gap.claim: Existing graph-clustering studies mostly assume discrete, unweighted, undirected graphs without self-loops, whereas real-world graphs can be more complex.

contributions.claim: GeneralACL extends ACL clustering to weighted, directed, and self-looped graphs.
HyperACL extends ACL clustering to hypergraphs with edge-dependent vertex weights.
The paper generalizes ACL's quadratic optimality to a wider range of complex graphs and hypergraphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Under two mild conditions, GeneralACL and HyperACL can identify a quadratically optimal cluster in terms of conductance.
Experiments are provided to validate the theoretical findings.
The authors report that their code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Local/seeded clustering aims to find compact clusters near starting instances.
Most prior graph-clustering work assumes discrete graphs, despite the complexity of real-world graphs.
The paper extends ACL clustering to complex graphs and hypergraphs and introduces GeneralACL and HyperACL.
Both algorithms are reported to identify quadratically optimal clusters under two mild conditions.
Experiments are provided to validate the theoretical findings.

source_observation.claim: Extending a classic clustering algorithm to weighted, directed, self-looped graphs and hypergraphs can broaden its applicability.

interpretation.claim: Algorithmic guarantees may remain useful when the structural assumptions of the original setting are relaxed.

application.claim: When clustering real-world relational data, consider methods that explicitly model graph complexity beyond unweighted undirected graphs.

exception.claim: The reported optimality depends on two mild conditions stated by the authors, whose details are not given in the abstract.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the two conditions required for the optimality result.
The abstract does not provide experimental datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or implementation details.
